source_facts.platform: T1 humanoid with eight passive skate-wheel DoFs
source_facts.learning: GMR-retargeted motion, processing, then separate AMP-PPO policies for Pump and Push Glide; wheel spin is excluded from imitation
source_facts.reported_forward_tests: Lateral and yaw commands are zero in the described quantitative gait tests; no high-speed large-beta drift benchmark is established
source_facts.data_release: Public code/motion download not located on the inspected project site; website redistribution is prohibited

GMR_name_caution: The paper calls GMR Gaussian Mixture Regression, while its reference6 cites General Motion Retargeting. This repository uses upstream/GMR GeneralMotionRetargeting, not an inferred Gaussian regression implementation.

relevance_to_current_experiment.contact_geometry: Directly relevant as an independently controlled wheel-profile ablation; cylinder slicing does not create a calibrated nonlinear tire law.
relevance_to_current_experiment.motion_prior: Plausible source of posture, leg coordination and load-transfer timing, after validating contact dynamics.
relevance_to_current_experiment.propulsion: Passive skating generates propulsion through legs; TRON1 has two driven wheels. Do not copy passive-wheel torque constraints into the driven robot.
relevance_to_current_experiment.speed_and_beta: Body and wheel heading offsets are useful features, but beta and path shape alone do not specify a feasible friction budget.
relevance_to_current_experiment.steady_turn_scaling: Our space0.08/time2 retarget reduces acceleration by0.02. Reusing a large human lean without adapting the acceleration/gravity ratio may be dynamically inconsistent.
relevance_to_current_experiment.unsupported_conclusion: Neither the paper nor the present tire-law runs establish that a human motion prior improves TRON1 drift.

arms: same task plus phase-aligned human posture tracking
same task plus AMP style reward
fixed: validated physical law and wheel geometry
task rewards and intended nonzero beta
proposed_fair_later_ablation.AMP_training_only_addition: Discriminator; wheel rotation is not an imitation target, while both wheel motors remain active.
demonstration_requirements: licensed source motion with sufficient travel and a real turning/sliding phase
separate left/right wheel rolling-plane headings and stance timing after GMR
explicit distinction between measured contacts and inferred contact labels
speed/curvature/acceleration compatibility with the retargeted robot
success_measures: core XY error and speed retention
loaded per-wheel patch slip and force utilization
any-wheel support gaps and torso angular high-frequency content
performance across identical validated contact-law conditions

recommendation: Use human motion as a conditional coordination prior, not as proof of tire accuracy or drift feasibility. Validate contact geometry/force coupling before starting the AMP comparison.
